title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
abstract: arXiv:2610.12872v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong individual task performance, yet still struggle to collaborate with users over extended, multi-turn interactions, for example by attempting solutions before understanding the user's needs or by failing to revise mistaken assumptions after receiving feedback. We propose Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM), a framework that addresses these challenges by explicitly training LLMs to anticipate user responses and to use those predictions to improve their own behavior. CToM drafts a response, predicts how the user will respond, and uses this prediction to guide internal revision before presenting a response. During training, the user's reply to each draft serves as the target for predicting the next turn, and we train the assistant to minimize the negative log-likelihood of that reply. translated_title: 协同心智理论：通过预测用户响应学习自我修订
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在单个任务上展现出强大的性能，但在长时间的多轮交互中仍然难以与用户协作，例如在理解用户需求之前就急于给出解决方案，或者在收到反馈后未能修正错误的假设。我们提出了协同心智理论，一个通过显式训练大语言模型预测用户响应，并利用这些预测来改进自身行为，从而应对上述挑战的框架。CToM先起草一个回复，预测用户将如何回应，并在最终呈现回复之前利用该预测来指导内部修订。在训练过程中，用户对每个草稿的回复被用作预测下一轮对话的目标，我们训练助手最小化该回复的负对数似然。我们将这一预测目标与组相对策略优化（GRPO）相结合，以同时优化任务表现……
tldr: 该论文提出协同心智理论（CToM）框架，通过训练大语言模型预测用户对草稿回复的响应，并利用该预测在回复前进行内部自我修订，同时结合GRPO优化，从而提升模型在多轮交互中与用户协作的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM), a framework that trains LLMs to anticipate user responses to their draft replies and use these predictions to guide internal self-revision before responding, combined with GRPO, to improve collaboration in extended multi-turn interactions.
